approach: Let `athena retry` accept a stale job, and teach `go` to rebuild its kept candidate on the new tip. (1) reading.rs: `earlier_attempt_with` accepts `Closed(Stale)`, and `carry` carries the stale outcome reason. (2) A new `Athena::stale_seed` in run/mod.rs runs inside `dispatch` for a "try again on <stale job>" request. It reads the job's recorded candidate (not the resume mark, which close.rs deletes for a stale job) and merges it with a new `athena_git::Git::merge_tree_report(old_base, head, candidate_commit)`. A clean merge goes to the existing `resume_candidate` with a new "merge" mode. That mode builds the tree with `merge_tree(old_base, new_prediction, old_candidate)` instead of replaying a diff, recomputes the change list as `diff_tree(p, merged_tree)`, and re-runs admission, checks, replay and the verifier through `check_and_verify`. No planner or producer runs, and landing is the unchanged `land::plan` path, which asserts that the landed fingerprint equals the verified one. A conflicted merge starts an ordinary producer run whose snapshot is seeded, via the existing `SnapshotRepo::BaseThenTree`, from a commit holding the conflicted merge tree (conflict markers in the conflicting files). The producer brief names the conflicting paths. If the candidate commit or base is gone or not an ancestor of the tip, or the request is pinned, the retry silently starts from the base, as a plain retry does. (3) Text: the retry help, the reader brief for a stale job, the producer brief's retry section for a conflict seed, close.rs's stale UI line, README, CHANGELOG and a new D159 appended to docs/decisions.md. (4) decisions.rs: re-pin the guard to the whole base file and add the "append at end of file" rule. snapshot.rs and candidate.rs are untouched, because D08 governs them in docs/decision-links.toml.

decisions.choice: Reuse `resume_candidate` with a merge mode for the clean case; do not write a new path.
decisions.reason: It already does the wanted job with no planner or producer run: it builds a candidate commit on the new prediction commit, runs admission, writes a resume mark and calls `check_and_verify`, which runs the checks, the replay and the verifier on that commit (run/mod.rs:524-651). Only how the tree is built differs: replaying `diff_tree(old_base, old_candidate)` over the new base (run/mod.rs:546-576) is only safe when nothing but `records/` changed (resume_seed, mod.rs:512), and a stale job by definition has other changes. A three-way `merge_tree` is the same operation `land::plan` uses for records (land.rs:117).

rejected.option: Land the old candidate through `land::plan` without re-verifying, since `merge_tree` is clean.
rejected.why: The merged tree has a different fingerprint than the one verified, so `plan` bails at land.rs:137-141. Landing unverified content is also what D10 forbids.

rejected.option: A separate `stale_retry` function that copies the checks and verifier calls.
rejected.why: It duplicates `check_and_verify`, so the two copies would drift.

decisions.choice: Read the candidate from the stale job's `candidate` record and derive the seed from it. Do not use the `ResumeMark` file.
decisions.reason: `settle_resume_marks` removes the job's own mark on every close except an environment failure (run/mod.rs:693), so a stale job has none. The candidate record is committed by `push_closing_records` and holds `base_commit`, `candidate_commit` and `changes`. The seed becomes a synthetic `ResumeMark` (stage Checks, empty `check_runs`, `report_gaps` and `left_criteria`). Those two lists are lost for a stale job, but the verifier re-judges every criterion.

rejected.option: Keep the resume mark when a job goes stale.
rejected.why: It changes `settle_resume_marks` for all closes and leaves files in the state directory for jobs nobody retries.

decisions.choice: On a conflict, seed the producer's work tree (`SnapshotRepo::BaseThenTree`) with a commit holding git's conflicted merge tree, conflict markers included. Pass the conflicting paths to the producer brief through a new `conflicts` field on `RetrySeed`.
decisions.reason: snapshot.rs is not touched (D08 governs it and the links file cannot be edited). `BaseThenTree` already materializes the visible files of any commit over the base, and the change list stays against the base (snapshot.rs:36-39, 97-100). Markers fail loudly if the producer leaves them in, where seeding with the candidate's version of the conflicting files would silently revert the tip's change. The producer's own `git diff` shows the tip's side, because the snapshot's base commit holds it.

rejected.why: It requires the job to be Rejected and the base to differ from the head only under `records/` (run/mod.rs:464-484). Neither holds for a stale job, and seeding from the old candidate directly would undo the tip's work.

rejected.option: Start the conflict case from the plain base with no seed.
rejected.why: This is what the repo does today and loses the finished work; acceptance criterion 3 requires seeding from the candidate.

decisions.choice: Add `Git::merge_tree_report` (clean tree, or conflicted tree plus conflicting paths, via `merge-tree --write-tree --name-only`). Leave `merge_tree` as is.
decisions.reason: `merge_tree` returns `None` on exit code 1 and drops the tree, which the conflict seed needs. Its callers (land.rs:117, gh/landing.rs:583 and 601, athena-git lib.rs:788) keep their exact behavior.

rejected.why: It touches three callers in the landing path for no gain.

decisions.choice: Re-pin the guard in decisions.rs to the whole base file (PINNED_LEN 359622, the base size in the brief; SHA-256 of those bytes). Add a rule: an entry that starts at or after the pin must have id = previous highest + 1. Every pin-related error message ends with 'append at end of file'.
decisions.reason: The real log has no D145 (D144 is followed by D146), so a consecutive-id rule applied from the old pin at D121 would fail on the real file. Pinning to the full base also makes criterion 5 true for the real log: D159 follows D158 directly. The existing messages ('changed', 'twice', 'ascend', 'shorter', 'no Provenance') keep their words, so the existing assertions hold.

rejected.option: Apply the consecutive rule only past a hard-coded id.
rejected.why: It hides the gap and leaves the pin stale.

rejected.option: Edit the log to fill D145.

decisions.choice: Write D159 without the phrases the supersession parser reads ('superseded by', 'supersedes', 'amends').
decisions.reason: `parse_supersessions` (backtest.rs:78-82) turns each such phrase followed by an id into a hit that must be listed in docs/decision-links.toml, which the brief bars from change. The entry cites D10 and states that it 'reverses' the left-out alternative (d) 'Automatic re-verification on the new base' because stale landings now recur with parallel jobs. D10 is not in any `[[governs]]` table, so no link is required.

rejected.option: Write 'Supersedes D10' with a new link.
rejected.why: The links file is out of scope, and (d) is only one of D10's alternatives, so D10 stands.

risks.risk: A conflict-seeded producer leaves conflict markers in a file and the markers reach landing.
risks.mitigation: The brief's conflict section names each conflicting path and says the markers must be resolved. The seed is a fail-safe, because markers never silently revert the tip's work. The checks, replay and the verifier run on whatever the producer leaves, and the lifecycle test checks that nothing lands before verification. A hard guard in `check_and_verify` is a possible follow-up. It is not in this plan, because candidate.rs and producer.rs, where it would sit, are D08-governed or outside the deliverables.

risks.risk: The kept candidate commit is an unreferenced object, so a git gc may have removed it.
risks.mitigation: `stale_seed` checks that both commits resolve with `rev_parse` and that the old base is an ancestor of the head. Otherwise it returns None and the retry starts from the base, as a plain retry does. A test covers the missing-commit case. This is the 'starts from the base when the candidate cannot be merged' behavior in the brief text.

risks.risk: The merged tree equals the tip because the change already landed, so the candidate is empty.
risks.mitigation: The merge mode fails the job with a clear reason ('the branch already holds the candidate's changes') through `self.failure`, with a unit test, and does not land an empty candidate.

risks.risk: `report_gaps` and `left_criteria` of the old run are lost for a stale job.
risks.mitigation: The synthetic `ResumeMark` uses empty lists. The verifier judges every criterion again, and the merge-mode test checks the verifier prompt carries the criteria.

risks.risk: The re-pin has the wrong hash or length and the real-log guard fails.
risks.mitigation: Step 8 reads the base file size and hash from the working copy before the append: `head -c 359622 docs/decisions.md | sha256sum` is the SHA, and `cargo test -p athena-cli decisions` prints the actual prefix hash on a mismatch. The new test also covers `check_log` on synthetic logs, so a wrong pin is caught.

risks.risk: D159 accidentally contains 'amends' or 'supersedes' and the supersession backtest flags an unlisted hit.
risks.mitigation: Step 8 checks the entry for those words with `grep -in` and the backtest test `cargo test -p athena-cli backtest` runs.

risks.risk: The branch moves again while the retry runs (parallel jobs).
risks.mitigation: The lifecycle tests drive the real Athena through `Fixture`, so the repository lock and the branch advance run for real. The retry's landing uses the existing three-attempt loop in `land_or_block`. Only the plan to land changes, so a branch that moves again during the retry goes stale again, as any job does.
